subject: plotOutliers() no longer compatible with Car package powerTrans()

messages.author: 417f8af07fb10e85
messages.subject: plotOutliers() no longer compatible with Car package powerTrans()
parts:
Hello Prof Collyer,

I hope all is well. 
I came across an issue yesterday that I thought would be good to inform you about.
When I run geomorph and am looking for outliers using plotOutliers(), I get an error: 

Error in int_abline(a = a, b = b, h = h, v = v, untf = untf, ...) :
  'a' and 'b' must be finite

When I use traceback() it seems as though the plotOutliers is trying to use the powerTrans() function from the Car package (i.e., bc <- powerTrans(D))

However, the recent update to Car has changed the powerTrans() cmd to powerTransform() – which no longer produces the bc$tranformed object when the bc <- powerTransform(D) is called. So, when the function attempts to calculate b, it can't and sets it to NULL. This then causes b to become non-finite and the plotOutliers() function to crash. 
Is this something that you might be able to repair? The plotOutliers function is super useful to detect strange individuals and landmarking errors; it would be great to get it working again.

What a pain it is when all the dependencies change to try and stay on top of all the updates. If I am wrong about the above - sorry about the confusion, but hopefully it's a pretty easy fix.

Many thanks and all the very best,

Hope this helps,

Denis

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] plotOutliers() no longer compatible with Car package powerTrans()
parts:
Dear Denis,

That error is caused by the graphics::abline function that plotOutliers uses, but which worked before.  It is not caused by the code used in plotOutliers.  We will have to figure out to work around it.  My suspicion is that a quantile like the upper confidence limit can be infinite and previously if this was the case, maybe the abline just did not add the line but now returns an error.  We could probably test first whether it is finite, but this was not an issue we had to address before.

Best,
Mike
